# Note Processor reference

Add these processors in a [Note Processor chain](note-processors.qmd).
**P Field** is the Csound score field to change: `p1` is the instrument,
`p2` the start, and `p3` the duration. Most numeric processors default to
`p4`. Check the target instrument's score format first; a processor that
expects a number cannot safely process text in that field. Chain order and
scope are explained in the [overview](note-processors.qmd).

## Field values

| Processor                   | Parameters                       | Effect                                                                |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **AddProcessor**            | P Field, Value                   | Adds a fixed number to every selected field.                          |
| **MultiplyProcessor**       | P Field, Value                   | Multiplies every selected field by a fixed number.                    |
| **EqualsProcessor**         | P Field, Value                   | Replaces the field with Value; `p3` also changes the note's duration. |
| **InversionProcessor**      | P Field, Value                   | Reflects numeric values around the given axis: `2 × Value − input`.   |
| **SwitchProcessor**         | P Field 1, P Field 2             | Exchanges two fields on each note.                                    |
| **RandomAddProcessor**      | P Field, Min, Max, optional Seed | Adds a random value between Min and Max to each note.                 |
| **RandomMultiplyProcessor** | P Field, Min, Max, optional Seed | Multiplies each note by a random factor in that range.                |
| **LineAddProcessor**        | P Field, time/value line         | Adds a value interpolated at each note's start.                       |
| **LineMultiplyProcessor**   | P Field, time/value line         | Multiplies by a value interpolated at each note's start.              |

**SwitchProcessor** follows Java Blue's field-range check: it rejects the
last p-field as well as missing fields. A swap between `p4` and `p5` therefore
requires a note with at least six p-fields.

For a repeatable random result, enable **Seed** and supply a seed. A line
is a sequence of beat/value pairs such as `0 0 4 1`: at beat zero its
value is zero and at beat four its value is one. Start the line no later
than the first note it processes. After the final pair, the last value
continues.

## Pitch and tuning

| Processor                 | Parameters                            | Effect                                                             |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **PchAddProcessor**       | P Field, Value                        | Adds a number of semitones to a Csound `pch` field.                |
| **PchInversionProcessor** | P Field, Value                        | Reflects a `pch` value around a `pch` axis.                        |
| **TuningProcessor**       | P Field, base frequency, scale ratios | Converts the field's octave and scale-degree value into frequency. |

These expect pitch encodings, not an arbitrary frequency or amplitude.
In particular, **TuningProcessor** uses the project's stored ratio list
and base frequency; test a short phrase after changing its scale.

## Note order and time

| Processor               | Parameters     | Effect                                                                                  |
| ----------------------- | -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **RetrogradeProcessor** | None           | Mirrors note start times across the phrase's end while retaining each duration.         |
| **RotateProcessor**     | Note Index     | Rotates sorted notes from that index and normalizes their new start times.              |
| **SubListProcessor**    | Start, End     | Keeps the one-based inclusive range of notes and normalizes it to start at zero.        |
| **TimeWarpProcessor**   | beat/tempo map | Converts start and end beats through its tempo map; both start and duration can change. |

**TimeWarpProcessor** uses beat/tempo pairs such as `0 60` for a constant
60 beats per minute. Preview the CSD after adding it, especially when
other processors or a SoundObject's Time Behavior also change timing.

## PythonProcessor

**PythonProcessor** stores code that edits a `noteList`. It requires a
working Java runtime session for asynchronous rendering. When the Java
runtime is unavailable, Blue cannot apply it during a render; an older
project may display it as deferred. Use the processor's code editor and
test with a small phrase before applying it at Score scope. The ordinary
TypeScript `process` path alone does not run the Python code.
